newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Labour body, Swiss groups urge Burma tour boycott.
newsitem.headline: Labour body, Swiss groups urge Burma tour boycott.

text.p: International labour union bodies based in Geneva and several Swiss non-governmental organisations on Tuesday appealed to businessmen and tourists for a travel and investment boycott of Burma.

The appeal was issued two weeks before the launch by the Burmese military government of a "Tourist Year" campaign which critics say is being promoted by advertisements for the country as "the mysterious land of golden pagodas."

It called on the Swiss people and political and economic leaders "to bring immediate support to the embattled Burmese democracy movement by refraining from travelling to Burma, and by refusing to cooperate in any way with the military regime."

It said the Rangoon government hoped the campaign would attract 250,000 travellers from around the world "whose tourist dollars will fill the state coffers emptied by the war the junta has been waging against its own people....
"In order to provide the necessary tourist infrastructure, the military government has comitted massive violations of human rights," the appeal declared.
"Hundreds of thousands of people have been forcibly relocated to provide space for new hotel complexes and business centres in time for the tourist year," it added.
"An unknown number of people, including women, children and the elderly, have been conscripted as forced labourers on roads, railways, airports and tourist sites."
Among organisations launching or supporting the appeal were global labour bodies representing workers in the food and catering industries, transport workers, and commercial and clerical employees.
